verdict: Apple's sales rose 5% to a June-quarter record $85.8B as Services hit an all-time high and iPad jumped 24% on its new models — and it kept $21.4B as profit even though iPhone sales dipped 1%.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: Apple's flagship phone — sales dipped 1% in the last full quarter before the iPhone 16 launch.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers — up 2%, helped by the MacBook Air with the M3 chip.

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: Tablets — the new iPad Pro with M4 and iPad Air with M2, launched in May, drove a 24% jump.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods and home devices — down 2% against a tough comparison.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, TV+ and advertising — an all-time record, up 14%.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing future iPhones, Macs, chips and services.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Stores, marketing and running the company day to day.

follow100Note: Services alone is $28.23 of every $100 Apple takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are net sales by product category, as Apple reports them.

takeaways.title: Services hit another record
takeaways.text: Services revenue reached $24.2B, an all-time high, up 14% — more than a quarter of everything Apple sells now comes from subscriptions, the App Store and other services.

takeaways.title: iPad bounced back
takeaways.text: iPad sales jumped 24% to $7.2B after the May launch of the redesigned iPad Pro and iPad Air — the lineup's first new models in over a year.

takeaways.title: Profit rose even with iPhone flat
takeaways.text: Net income rose 8% to $21.4B and EPS reached $1.40, helped by the high-margin Services mix; Apple Intelligence, unveiled in June, was still to come in the fall.
